## Access Tracking

### getAccessHistoryCluster

`accessTracking.getAccessHistoryCluster`

Return Database Access History for One Cluster by Cluster Name: returns the access logs of one cluster identified by the cluster's name

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.accessTracking.getAccessHistoryCluster({ groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718', clusterName: 'Cluster0' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `authResult` | `boolean` | No | Flag that indicates whether the response returns the successful authentication attempts only. |
| `clusterName` | `string` | Yes | Human-readable label that identifies the cluster. |
| `end` | `number` | No | Date and time when to stop retrieving database history. If you specify **end**, you must also specify **start**. This parameter uses UNIX epoch time in milliseconds. |
| `ipAddress` | `string` | No | One Internet Protocol address that attempted to authenticate with the database. |
| `nLogs` | `number` | No | Maximum number of lines from the log to return. |
| `start` | `number` | No | Date and time when MongoDB Cloud begins retrieving database history. If you specify **start**, you must also specify **end**. This parameter uses UNIX epoch time in milliseconds. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `accessLogs` | `object[] \| null` | No | Authentication attempt, one per object, made against the cluster. |

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="accessLogs full type">

```ts
{
  authResult?: boolean | null,
  authSource?: string | null,
  failureReason?: string | null,
  groupId?: string | null,
  hostname?: string | null,
  ipAddress?: string | null,
  logLine?: string | null,
  timestamp?: string | null,
  username?: string | null
}[] | null
```
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

### getAccessHistoryProcess

`accessTracking.getAccessHistoryProcess`

Return Database Access History for One Cluster by Hostname: returns the access logs of one cluster identified by the cluster's hostname

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.accessTracking.getAccessHistoryProcess({ groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718', hostname: 'example' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `authResult` | `boolean` | No | Flag that indicates whether the response returns the successful authentication attempts only. |
| `end` | `number` | No | Date and time when to stop retrieving database history. If you specify **end**, you must also specify **start**. This parameter uses UNIX epoch time in milliseconds. |
| `hostname` | `string` | Yes | Fully qualified domain name or IP address of the MongoDB host that stores the log files that you want to download. |
| `ipAddress` | `string` | No | One Internet Protocol address that attempted to authenticate with the database. |
| `nLogs` | `number` | No | Maximum number of lines from the log to return. |
| `start` | `number` | No | Date and time when MongoDB Cloud begins retrieving database history. If you specify **start**, you must also specify **end**. This parameter uses UNIX epoch time in milliseconds. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `accessLogs` | `object[] \| null` | No | Authentication attempt, one per object, made against the cluster. |

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="accessLogs full type">

```ts
{
  authResult?: boolean | null,
  authSource?: string | null,
  failureReason?: string | null,
  groupId?: string | null,
  hostname?: string | null,
  ipAddress?: string | null,
  logLine?: string | null,
  timestamp?: string | null,
  username?: string | null
}[] | null
```
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Activity Feed

Return Pre-Filtered Activity Feed Link for One Project: returns a pre-filtered activity feed link for the specified project based on the provided date range and event types

### getOrgActivityFeed

`activityFeed.getOrgActivityFeed`

Return Pre-Filtered Activity Feed Link for One Organization: returns a pre-filtered activity feed link for the specified organization based on the provided date range and event types

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.activityFeed.getOrgActivityFeed({ orgId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |

| `orgId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the organization that contains your projects. Use the [`/orgs`](#tag/Organizations/operation/listOrganizations) endpoint to retrieve all organizations to which the authenticated user has access. |

## Ai Model Api Keys

### createGroupModelKey

`aiModelApiKeys.createGroupModelKey`

Create New AI Model API Key: create a new AI model API key for the given group

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.aiModelApiKeys.createGroupModelKey({
	groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718',
	cloud: 'ANY',
	geography: 'ANY',
	name: 'Cluster0',
});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `cloud` | `ANY` | Yes | Cloud provider scope for this API key. Use "ANY" for a cloud-agnostic scope. Additional cloud values will be supported in future API versions. |
| `geography` | `ANY \| EU \| US` | Yes | Geography scope for this API key. Use "ANY" for a geography-agnostic scope. Additional geography values will be supported in future API versions. |
| `name` | `string` | Yes | A name for the new API key that will be created. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `apiKeyId` | `string \| null` | No | Identifier used to reference this API key in admin API calls. |
| `cloud` | `string \| null` | No | Cloud provider scope for this API key. Use "ANY" for cloud-agnostic scope. |
| `createdAt` | `string \| null` | No | UTC date when the API key was created. This parameter is formatted as an ISO 8601 timestamp. |
| `createdBy` | `string \| null` | No | Name of the user that created this API key. If no user name is available, the user ID is returned. |
| `endpoint` | `string \| null` | No | Server-computed endpoint hostname derived from `cloud` and `geography`. This field is read-only and must not be supplied in request bodies. |
| `geography` | `string \| null` | No | Geography scope for this API key. Use "ANY" for geography-agnostic scope. |
| `groupId` | `string \| null` | No | ID of the Atlas group this API key belongs to. |
| `lastUsedAt` | `string \| null \| null` | No | UTC date when the API key was last used. This parameter is formatted as an ISO 8601 timestamp. |
| `maskedSecret` | `string \| null` | No | A partially obfuscated version of the API key secret returned when the API key was created. |
| `name` | `string \| null` | No | Arbitrary string identifier assigned to this API key for convenient identification. |
| `secret` | `string \| null \| null` | No | The full API key secret used for interacting with the embedding / reranking service. Note: this will only be fully populated in the response to a create API key request. Responses to get, list, and update requests will not include the secret. |
| `status` | `string \| null` | No | A string describing the current status of the API key. |

### getOrgRateLimits

`aiModelRateLimits.getOrgRateLimits`

Return Single AI Model Rate Limit for One Organization: retrieve a single scoped AI model rate limit for the given organization

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.aiModelRateLimits.getOrgRateLimits({
	orgId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718',
	cloud: 'ANY',
	geography: 'ANY',
	modelGroupName: 'example',
});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `orgId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the organization that contains your projects. Use the [`/orgs`](#tag/Organizations/operation/listOrganizations) endpoint to retrieve all organizations to which the authenticated user has access. |
| `cloud` | `ANY` | Yes | Cloud provider scope. Must be "ANY". Additional values will be supported in future API versions. |
| `geography` | `ANY` | Yes | Geography scope. Must be "ANY". Additional values will be supported in future API versions. |
| `modelGroupName` | `string` | Yes | The name of the model group to be retrieved. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `cloud` | `string \| null` | No | Cloud provider scope for this rate limit. Use "ANY" for cloud-agnostic scope. |
| `endpoint` | `string \| null` | No | Server-computed endpoint hostname derived from `cloud` and `geography`. This field is read-only and must not be supplied in request bodies. |
| `geography` | `string \| null` | No | Geography scope for this rate limit. Use "ANY" for geography-agnostic scope. |
| `modelGroupName` | `string \| null` | No | Identifier used to reference this model group. |
| `modelNames` | `string[] \| null` | No | List of embedding model names included in this model group. |
| `requestsPerMinuteLimit` | `number \| null` | No | The number of requests per minute allowed for this model group. Must be a positive integer. Cannot be more than the organization level limit for this group model. |
| `tokensPerMinuteLimit` | `number \| null` | No | The number of tokens per minute allowed for this model group. Must be a positive integer. Cannot be more than the organization level limit for this group model. |

### deleteAlertConfig

`alertConfigurations.deleteAlertConfig`

Remove One Alert Configuration from One Project: removes one alert configuration from the specified project

**Risk:** `destructive` · **Irreversible**

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.alertConfigurations.deleteAlertConfig({ groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718', alertConfigId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `alertConfigId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the alert configuration. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `success` | `true` | Yes | MongoDBAtlas accepted the call; it answered with no body (or an empty object). |

### getAlertConfigs

`alertConfigurations.getAlertConfigs`

Return All Alert Configurations Set for One Alert: returns all alert configurations set for the specified alert (paged with pageNum / itemsPerPage)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.alertConfigurations.getAlertConfigs({ groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718', alertId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `includeCount` | `boolean` | No | Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud calculates the total number of items for the response. When set to `false`, MongoDB Cloud may skip an additional count operation. The response may still include `totalCount` when the count is available without additional calculation. |
| `itemsPerPage` | `number` | No | Number of items that the response returns per page. |
| `pageNum` | `number` | No | Number of the page that displays the current set of the total objects that the response returns. |
| `alertId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the alert. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `links` | `object[] \| null` | No | List of one or more Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) that point to API sub-resources, related API resources, or both. RFC 5988 outlines these relationships. |
| `results` | `object[] \| null` | No | List of returned documents that MongoDB Cloud provides when completing this request. |
| `totalCount` | `number \| null` | No | Total number of documents available. When `includeCount` is set to `false`, MongoDB Cloud may omit this value or return it when the count is available without additional calculation. The total number is an estimate and may not be exact. |

### listAlertConfigs

`alertConfigurations.listAlertConfigs`

Return All Alert Configurations in One Project: returns all alert configurations for one project (paged with pageNum / itemsPerPage)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.alertConfigurations.listAlertConfigs({ groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `includeCount` | `boolean` | No | Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud calculates the total number of items for the response. When set to `false`, MongoDB Cloud may skip an additional count operation. The response may still include `totalCount` when the count is available without additional calculation. |
| `itemsPerPage` | `number` | No | Number of items that the response returns per page. |
| `pageNum` | `number` | No | Number of the page that displays the current set of the total objects that the response returns. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `links` | `object[] \| null` | No | List of one or more Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) that point to API sub-resources, related API resources, or both. RFC 5988 outlines these relationships. |
| `results` | `object[] \| null` | No | List of returned documents that MongoDB Cloud provides when completing this request. |
| `totalCount` | `number \| null` | No | Total number of documents available. When `includeCount` is set to `false`, MongoDB Cloud may omit this value or return it when the count is available without additional calculation. The total number is an estimate and may not be exact. |

### listMatcherFieldNames

`alertConfigurations.listMatcherFieldNames`

Return All Alert Configuration Matchers Field Names: get all field names that the `matchers.fieldName` parameter accepts when you create or update an Alert Configuration

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.alertConfigurations.listMatcherFieldNames({});
```

### toggleAlertConfig

`alertConfigurations.toggleAlertConfig`

Toggle State of One Alert Configuration in One Project: enables or disables the specified alert configuration in the specified project

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.alertConfigurations.toggleAlertConfig({ groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718', alertConfigId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `alertConfigId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the alert configuration that triggered this alert. |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | No | Flag that indicates whether to enable or disable the specified alert configuration in the specified project. |



**Output:** `object`

### updateAlertConfig

`alertConfigurations.updateAlertConfig`

Update One Alert Configuration in One Project: updates one alert configuration in the specified project

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.alertConfigurations.updateAlertConfig({
	groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718',
	alertConfigId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718',
	body: {
		eventTypeName: 'CREDIT_CARD_ABOUT_TO_EXPIRE',
		notifications: [{ typeName: 'DATADOG' }],
	},
});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `alertConfigId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the alert configuration. |
| `body` | `object` | Yes | — |

---

## Alerts

### acknowledgeAlert

`alerts.acknowledgeAlert`

Acknowledge One Alert from One Project: confirms receipt of one existing alert

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.alerts.acknowledgeAlert({ groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718', alertId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `alertId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the alert. |
| `acknowledgedUntil` | `string` | No | Date and time until which this alert has been acknowledged. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. The resource returns this parameter if a MongoDB User previously acknowledged this alert. |

## Atlas Search

### createClusterSearchDeployment

`atlasSearch.createClusterSearchDeployment`

Create Search Nodes: creates Search Nodes for the specified cluster

**Risk:** `destructive`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.atlasSearch.createClusterSearchDeployment({
	groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718',
	clusterName: 'Cluster0',
	specs: [{ instanceSize: 'S10_HIGHCPU' }],
});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `clusterName` | `string` | Yes | Label that identifies the cluster to create Search Nodes for. |
| `autoScaling` | `object` | No | Settings that let Atlas change the Search Node tier on its own. Bounds apply to the whole deployment, and Atlas scales each region and shard independently within them. Omit to keep autoscaling off. |
| `defaultNodeCount` | `number \| null` | No | Default number of Search Nodes per region. Applied to a region without an explicit override. |
| `specs` | `object[]` | Yes | List of settings that configure the Search Nodes for your cluster. Provide one element per region when configuring asymmetric deployments; a single element applies to all regions. |

## Auditing

### getGroupAuditLog

`auditing.getGroupAuditLog`

Return Auditing Configuration for One Project: returns the auditing configuration for the specified project

**Risk:** `read`

```ts

```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|

| `configurationType` | `string \| null` | No | Human-readable label that displays how to configure the audit filter. |
| `enabled` | `boolean \| null` | No | Flag that indicates whether someone enabled database auditing for the specified project. |

**Risk:** `write`

Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `cloudProvider` | `AWS` | Yes | Human-readable label that identifies the cloud provider for the private endpoint to create. |
| `regionName` | `US_GOV_WEST_1 \| US_GOV_EAST_1 \| US_EAST_1 \| US_EAST_2 \| US_WEST_1 \| US_WEST_2 \| CA_CENTRAL_1 \| EU_NORTH_1 \| EU_WEST_1 \| EU_WEST_2 \| EU_WEST_3 \| EU_CENTRAL_1 \| AP_EAST_1 \| AP_NORTHEAST_1 \| AP_NORTHEAST_2 \| AP_NORTHEAST_3 \| AP_SOUTHEAST_1 \| AP_SOUTHEAST_2 \| AP_SOUTHEAST_3 \| AP_SOUTH_1 \| SA_EAST_1 \| CN_NORTH_1 \| CN_NORTHWEST_1 \| ME_SOUTH_1 \| AF_SOUTH_1 \| EU_SOUTH_1 \| GLOBAL` | No | Cloud provider region of the S3 bucket that the Object Storage private endpoint accesses. For same-region endpoints, this is also the region where the VPC interface endpoint is deployed. |
| `vpcRegionName` | `US_GOV_WEST_1 \| US_GOV_EAST_1 \| US_EAST_1 \| US_EAST_2 \| US_WEST_1 \| US_WEST_2 \| CA_CENTRAL_1 \| EU_NORTH_1 \| EU_WEST_1 \| EU_WEST_2 \| EU_WEST_3 \| EU_CENTRAL_1 \| AP_EAST_1 \| AP_NORTHEAST_1 \| AP_NORTHEAST_2 \| AP_NORTHEAST_3 \| AP_SOUTHEAST_1 \| AP_SOUTHEAST_2 \| AP_SOUTHEAST_3 \| AP_SOUTH_1 \| SA_EAST_1 \| CN_NORTH_1 \| CN_NORTHWEST_1 \| ME_SOUTH_1 \| AF_SOUTH_1 \| EU_SOUTH_1 \| GLOBAL` | No | Cloud provider region in which the VPC interface endpoint is deployed. Omit to deploy the interface endpoint in the same region as the S3 bucket (same-region endpoint). Set to a region different from `regionName` to create a cross-region endpoint. |

### createBackupRestoreJob

`cloudBackups.createBackupRestoreJob`

Create One Restore Job of One Cluster: restores one snapshot of one cluster from the specified project

**Risk:** `destructive` · **Irreversible**

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.cloudBackups.createBackupRestoreJob({ groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718', clusterName: 'Cluster0', deliveryType: 'automated' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `clusterName` | `string` | Yes | Human-readable label that identifies the cluster. |
| `deliveryType` | `automated \| download \| pointInTime` | Yes | Human-readable label that categorizes the restore job to create. |
| `oplogInc` | `number` | No | Oplog operation number from which you want to restore this snapshot. This number represents the second part of an Oplog timestamp. The resource returns this parameter when `"deliveryType" : "pointInTime"` and `oplogTs` exceeds `0`. |
| `oplogTs` | `number` | No | Date and time from which you want to restore this snapshot. This parameter expresses this timestamp in the number of seconds that have elapsed since the UNIX epoch. This number represents the first part of an Oplog timestamp. The resource returns this parameter when `"deliveryType" : "pointInTime"` and `oplogTs` exceeds `0`. |
| `pointInTimeUTCSeconds` | `number` | No | Date and time from which MongoDB Cloud restored this snapshot. This parameter expresses this timestamp in the number of seconds that have elapsed since the UNIX epoch. The resource returns this parameter when `"deliveryType" : "pointInTime"` and `pointInTimeUTCSeconds` exceeds `0`. |
| `snapshotId` | `string` | No | Unique 24-hexadecimal character string that identifies the snapshot. |
| `targetClusterName` | `string` | No | Human-readable label that identifies the target cluster to which the restore job restores the snapshot. The resource returns this parameter when `"deliveryType":` `"automated"`. Required for `automated` and `pointInTime` restore types. |
| `targetGroupId` | `string` | No | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the target project for the specified `targetClusterName`. Required for `automated` and `pointInTime` restore types. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `cancelled` | `boolean \| null` | No | Flag that indicates whether someone canceled this restore job. |
| `components` | `object[] \| null` | No | Information on the restore job for each replica set in the sharded cluster. |
| `deliveryType` | `string \| null` | No | Human-readable label that categorizes the restore job to create. |
| `deliveryUrl` | `string[] \| null` | No | One or more Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) that point to the compressed snapshot files for manual download. MongoDB Cloud returns this parameter when `"deliveryType" : "download"`. |
| `desiredTimestamp` | `object \| null` | No | BSON timestamp that indicates when the checkpoint token entry in the oplog occurred. |
| `expired` | `boolean \| null` | No | Flag that indicates whether the restore job expired. |
| `expiresAt` | `string \| null` | No | Date and time when the restore job expires. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. |
| `failed` | `boolean \| null` | No | Flag that indicates whether the restore job failed. |
| `finishedAt` | `string \| null` | No | Date and time when the restore job completed. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. |
| `id` | `string \| null` | No | Unique 24-hexadecimal character string that identifies the restore job. |
| `links` | `object[] \| null` | No | List of one or more Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) that point to API sub-resources, related API resources, or both. RFC 5988 outlines these relationships. |
| `oplogInc` | `number \| null` | No | Oplog operation number from which you want to restore this snapshot. This number represents the second part of an Oplog timestamp. The resource returns this parameter when `"deliveryType" : "pointInTime"` and `oplogTs` exceeds `0`. |
| `oplogTs` | `number \| null` | No | Date and time from which you want to restore this snapshot. This parameter expresses this timestamp in the number of seconds that have elapsed since the UNIX epoch. This number represents the first part of an Oplog timestamp. The resource returns this parameter when `"deliveryType" : "pointInTime"` and `oplogTs` exceeds `0`. |
| `pointInTimeUTCSeconds` | `number \| null` | No | Date and time from which MongoDB Cloud restored this snapshot. This parameter expresses this timestamp in the number of seconds that have elapsed since the UNIX epoch. The resource returns this parameter when `"deliveryType" : "pointInTime"` and `pointInTimeUTCSeconds` exceeds `0`. |
| `privateDownloadDeliveryUrls` | `object[] \| null` | No | One or more Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) that point to the compressed snapshot files for manual download and the corresponding private endpoint(s). MongoDB Cloud returns this parameter when `"deliveryType" : "download"` and the download can be performed privately. |
| `snapshotId` | `string \| null` | No | Unique 24-hexadecimal character string that identifies the snapshot. |
| `targetClusterName` | `string \| null` | No | Human-readable label that identifies the target cluster to which the restore job restores the snapshot. The resource returns this parameter when `"deliveryType":` `"automated"`. Required for `automated` and `pointInTime` restore types. |
| `targetGroupId` | `string \| null` | No | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the target project for the specified `targetClusterName`. Required for `automated` and `pointInTime` restore types. |
| `timestamp` | `string \| null` | No | Date and time when MongoDB Cloud took the snapshot associated with `snapshotId`. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. |

### updateBackupSchedule

`cloudBackups.updateBackupSchedule`

Update Cloud Backup Schedule for One Cluster: updates the cloud backup schedule for one cluster within the specified project

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.cloudBackups.updateBackupSchedule({
	groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718',
	clusterName: 'Cluster0',
	policies: [{
		policyItems: [{
			frequencyInterval: 1,
			frequencyType: 'daily',
			retentionUnit: 'days',
			retentionValue: 1,
		}],
	}],
});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `clusterName` | `string` | Yes | Human-readable label that identifies the cluster. |
| `autoCopySettingsEnabled` | `boolean` | No | Flag that indicates whether the copy settings are automatically managed by MongoDB Cloud and sync to the cluster topology. |
| `autoExportEnabled` | `boolean` | No | Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud automatically exports Cloud Backup Snapshots to the Export Bucket. |
| `copyPolicyItemsEnabled` | `boolean` | No | Flag that indicates whether copy settings use `copyPolicyItems` instead of `frequencies`. When true, requests must supply `copyPolicyItems` and responses return `copyPolicyItems` only. When false or omitted, requests must supply `frequencies` and responses return `frequencies` only. |
| `copySettings` | `object[]` | No | List that contains a document for each copy setting item in the desired backup policy. |
| `deleteCopiedBackups` | `object[]` | No | List that contains a document for each deleted copy setting whose backup copies you want to delete. |
| `deleteCopySnapshots` | `boolean` | No | Flag that indicates whether to delete Snapshot copies that MongoDB Cloud took previously when their associated `copyPolicyItems` are removed from a `copySetting`. This option requires `copyPolicyItemsEnabled` to be true. |
| `deleteSnapshots` | `boolean` | No | Flag that indicates whether to delete Snapshots that MongoDB Cloud took previously when deleting the associated backup policy. |
| `export` | `object` | No | Policy for automatically exporting Cloud Backup Snapshots. |
| `extraRetentionSettings` | `object[]` | No | List that contains a document for each extra retention setting item in the desired backup policy. |
| `policies` | `object[]` | Yes | Rules set for this backup schedule. |
| `referenceHourOfDay` | `number` | No | Hour of day in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) that represents when MongoDB Cloud takes the Snapshot. |
| `referenceMinuteOfHour` | `number` | No | Minute of the `referenceHourOfDay` that represents when MongoDB Cloud takes the Snapshot. |
| `restoreWindowDays` | `number` | No | Number of previous days that you can restore back to with Continuous Cloud Backup accuracy. You must specify a positive, non-zero integer. This parameter applies to continuous Cloud Backups only. |
| `updateCopySnapshots` | `boolean` | No | Flag that indicates whether to apply the retention changes for updated copy policy items to Snapshot copies that MongoDB Cloud took previously. |
| `updateSnapshots` | `boolean` | No | Flag that indicates whether to apply the retention changes in the updated backup policy to Snapshots that MongoDB Cloud took previously. |
| `useOrgAndGroupNamesInExportPrefix` | `boolean` | No | Flag that indicates whether to use organization and project names instead of organization and project UUIDs in the path to the metadata files that MongoDB Cloud uploads to your Export Bucket. |

### updateBackupSnapshot

`cloudBackups.updateBackupSnapshot`

Update Expiration Date for One Cloud Backup: changes the expiration date for one cloud backup snapshot for one cluster in the specified project, the requesting Service Account or API Key must have the Project Backup Manager role

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.cloudBackups.updateBackupSnapshot({
	groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718',
	clusterName: 'Cluster0',
	snapshotId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718',
	retentionUnit: 'DAYS',
	retentionValue: 1,
});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `clusterName` | `string` | Yes | Human-readable label that identifies the cluster. |
| `snapshotId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the desired snapshot. |
| `retentionUnit` | `DAYS \| WEEKS \| MONTHS \| YEARS` | Yes | Quantity of time in which MongoDB Cloud measures snapshot retention. |
| `retentionValue` | `number` | Yes | Number that indicates the amount of days, weeks, months, or years that MongoDB Cloud retains the snapshot. For less frequent policy items, MongoDB Cloud requires that you specify a value greater than or equal to the value specified for more frequent policy items. If the hourly policy item specifies a retention of two days, specify two days or greater for the retention of the weekly policy item. |

| `copyProtectionEnabled` | `boolean \| null` | No | Flag that indicates whether to prevent cluster users from deleting backups copied to other regions, even if those additional snapshot regions are removed. If unspecified, this value defaults to false. |

| `encryptionAtRestEnabled` | `boolean \| null` | No | Flag that indicates whether Encryption at Rest using Customer Key Management is required for all clusters with a Backup Compliance Policy. If unspecified, this value defaults to false. |
| `onDemandPolicyItem` | `object \| null` | No | Specifications for on-demand policy. |
| `pitEnabled` | `boolean \| null` | No | Flag that indicates whether the cluster uses Continuous Cloud Backups with a Backup Compliance Policy. If unspecified, this value defaults to false. |
| `projectId` | `string \| null` | No | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the project for the Backup Compliance Policy. |
| `restoreWindowDays` | `number \| null` | No | Number of previous days that you can restore back to with Continuous Cloud Backup with a Backup Compliance Policy. You must specify a positive, non-zero integer, and the maximum retention window can't exceed the hourly retention time. This parameter applies only to Continuous Cloud Backups with a Backup Compliance Policy. |
| `scheduledPolicyItems` | `object[] \| null` | No | List that contains the specifications for one scheduled policy. |
| `state` | `string \| null` | No | Label that indicates the state of the Backup Compliance Policy settings. MongoDB Cloud ignores this setting when you enable or update the Backup Compliance Policy settings. |
| `updatedDate` | `string \| null` | No | ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC that indicates when the user updated the Data Protection Policy settings. MongoDB Cloud ignores this setting when you enable or update the Backup Compliance Policy settings. |
| `updatedUser` | `string \| null` | No | Email address that identifies the user who updated the Backup Compliance Policy settings. MongoDB Cloud ignores this email setting when you enable or update the Backup Compliance Policy settings. |

## Cloud Migration Service

### createGroupLiveMigration

`cloudMigrationService.createGroupLiveMigration`

Create One Migration for One Local Managed Cluster to MongoDB Atlas: migrate one cluster that Cloud or Ops Manager manages to MongoDB Atlas

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.cloudMigrationService.createGroupLiveMigration({
	groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718',
	destination: { clusterName: 'Cluster0', groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718', hostnameSchemaType: 'PUBLIC' },
	migrationHosts: ['example'],
	source: {
		clusterName: 'Cluster0',
		groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718',
		managedAuthentication: true,
		ssl: true,
	},
});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `destination` | `object` | Yes | Document that describes the destination of the migration. |
| `dropDestinationData` | `boolean` | No | Flag that indicates whether the migration process drops all collections from the destination cluster before the migration starts. |
| `migrationHosts` | `string[]` | Yes | List of migration hosts used for this migration. |
| `sharding` | `object` | No | Document that configures sharding on the destination cluster when migrating from a replica set source to a sharded cluster destination on MongoDB 6.0 or higher. If you don't wish to shard any collections on the destination cluster, leave this empty. |
| `source` | `object` | Yes | Document that describes the source of the migration. |

| `migrationHosts` | `string[] \| null` | No | List of hosts running MongoDB Agents. These Agents can transfer your MongoDB data between one source and one destination cluster. |
| `readyForCutover` | `boolean \| null` | No | Flag that indicates the migrated cluster can be cut over to MongoDB Atlas. |
| `status` | `string \| null \| null` | No | Progress made in migrating one cluster to MongoDB Atlas. `NEW`: Someone scheduled a local cluster migration to MongoDB Atlas. `FAILED`: The cluster migration to MongoDB Atlas failed. `COMPLETE`: The cluster migration to MongoDB Atlas succeeded. `EXPIRED`: MongoDB Atlas prepares to begin the cut over of the migrating cluster when source and destination clusters have almost synchronized. If `"readyForCutover" : true`, this synchronization starts a timer of 120 hours. You can extend this timer. If  |

### deleteCluster

`clusters.deleteCluster`

Remove One Cluster from One Project: removes one cluster from the specified project

**Risk:** `destructive` · **Irreversible**

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.clusters.deleteCluster({ groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718', clusterName: 'Cluster0' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `clusterName` | `string` | Yes | Human-readable label that identifies the cluster. |
| `retainBackups` | `boolean` | No | Flag that indicates whether to retain backup snapshots for the deleted dedicated cluster. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `success` | `true` | Yes | MongoDBAtlas accepted the call; it answered with no body (or an empty object). |

### getClusterAdaptiveSettings

`clusters.getClusterAdaptiveSettings`

Return Adaptive Settings for One Cluster: returns the Adaptive Settings for the specified cluster, including client-provided overrides and the effective settings derived from those overrides and Atlas-managed defaults

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.clusters.getClusterAdaptiveSettings({ groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718', clusterName: 'Cluster0' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `clusterName` | `string` | Yes | Human-readable label that identifies the cluster. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `adaptiveSettingsOverrides` | `object \| null` | No | Map of customer-specified overrides for Adaptive Settings, applied on a best-effort basis. Each supported entry that you specify in this object takes precedence over the corresponding Atlas-managed default. For example, if a setting is enabled by default, you can add an override to disable it for your cluster. |
| `effectiveAdaptiveSettings` | `object \| null` | No | The effective state of Adaptive Settings currently applied to your cluster, based on your overrides and Atlas-managed defaults. Atlas-managed defaults can vary by MongoDB version, so the same setting may default differently across clusters running different versions. If you set an override for a setting that your cluster's current MongoDB version doesn't support, the override doesn't take effect and the effective value reflects the Atlas-managed default instead. |

### updateCluster

### updateClusterAdaptiveSettings

`clusters.updateClusterAdaptiveSettings`

Update Adaptive Settings for One Cluster: updates the client-provided Adaptive Settings overrides for the specified cluster and returns the resulting Adaptive Settings, including the effective settings derived from those overrides and Atlas-managed defaults

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.clusters.updateClusterAdaptiveSettings({ groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718', clusterName: 'Cluster0' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `clusterName` | `string` | Yes | Human-readable label that identifies the cluster. |
| `adaptiveSettingsOverrides` | `object` | No | Map of customer-specified overrides for Adaptive Settings, applied on a best-effort basis. Each supported entry that you specify in this object takes precedence over the corresponding Atlas-managed default. For example, if a setting is enabled by default, you can add an override to disable it for your cluster. |

```ts
{
}
```

**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `adaptiveSettingsOverrides` | `object \| null` | No | Map of customer-specified overrides for Adaptive Settings, applied on a best-effort basis. Each supported entry that you specify in this object takes precedence over the corresponding Atlas-managed default. For example, if a setting is enabled by default, you can add an override to disable it for your cluster. |
| `effectiveAdaptiveSettings` | `object \| null` | No | The effective state of Adaptive Settings currently applied to your cluster, based on your overrides and Atlas-managed defaults. Atlas-managed defaults can vary by MongoDB version, so the same setting may default differently across clusters running different versions. If you set an override for a setting that your cluster's current MongoDB version doesn't support, the override doesn't take effect and the effective value reflects the Atlas-managed default instead. |

`clusters.updateProcessArgs`

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.clusters.updateProcessArgs({ groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718', clusterName: 'Cluster0' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `clusterName` | `string` | Yes | Human-readable label that identifies the cluster. |
| `changeStreamOptionsPreAndPostImagesExpireAfterSeconds` | `number` | No | The minimum pre- and post-image retention time in seconds. |
| `chunkMigrationConcurrency` | `number` | No | Number of threads on the source shard and the receiving shard for chunk migration. The number of threads should not exceed the half the total number of CPU cores in the sharded cluster. |
| `customOpensslCipherConfigTls12` | `(TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 \| TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256)[]` | No | The custom OpenSSL cipher suite list for TLS 1.2. Requires `tlsCipherConfigMode` = `CUSTOM`; when `tlsCipherConfigMode` is omitted, supplying a non-empty list infers `CUSTOM`. |
| `customOpensslCipherConfigTls13` | `(TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 \| TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256 \| TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 \| TLS_AES_128_CCM_SHA256)[]` | No | The custom OpenSSL cipher suite list for TLS 1.3. Requires `tlsCipherConfigMode` = `CUSTOM`; when `tlsCipherConfigMode` is omitted, supplying a non-empty list infers `CUSTOM`. |

| `defaultWriteConcern` | `string` | No | Default level of acknowledgment requested from MongoDB for write operations when none is specified by the driver. |
| `javascriptEnabled` | `boolean` | No | Flag that indicates whether the cluster allows execution of operations that perform server-side executions of JavaScript. When using 8.0+, we recommend disabling server-side JavaScript and using operators of aggregation pipeline as more performant alternative. |
| `minimumEnabledTlsProtocol` | `TLS1_2 \| TLS1_3` | No | Minimum Transport Layer Security (TLS) version that the cluster accepts for incoming connections. |
| `noTableScan` | `boolean` | No | Flag that indicates whether the cluster disables executing any query that requires a collection scan to return results. |
| `oplogMinRetentionHours` | `number \| null` | No | Minimum retention window for cluster's oplog expressed in hours. A value of null indicates that the cluster uses the default minimum oplog window that MongoDB Cloud calculates. |
| `oplogSizeMB` | `number \| null` | No | Storage limit of cluster's oplog expressed in megabytes. A value of null indicates that the cluster uses the default oplog size that MongoDB Cloud calculates. |
| `queryStatsLogVerbosity` | `number` | No | May be set to 1 (disabled) or 3 (enabled). When set to 3, Atlas will include redacted and anonymized `$queryStats` output in MongoDB logs. `$queryStats` output does not contain literals or field values. Enabling this setting might impact the performance of your cluster. |
| `sampleRefreshIntervalBIConnector` | `number` | No | Interval in seconds at which the mongosqld process re-samples data to create its relational schema. |
| `sampleSizeBIConnector` | `number` | No | Number of documents per database to sample when gathering schema information. |
| `tlsCipherConfigMode` | `CUSTOM \| DEFAULT` | No | The TLS cipher suite configuration mode. The default mode uses the default cipher suites. The custom mode allows you to specify custom cipher suites for both TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3. |
| `transactionLifetimeLimitSeconds` | `number` | No | Lifetime, in seconds, of multi-document transactions. Atlas considers the transactions that exceed this limit as expired and so aborts them through a periodic clean-up process. |

For versions available in a specific project, see the linked documentation or use the API endpoint for [project LTS versions endpoint](#tag/Pro |
| `mongoDBVersion` | `string \| null` | No | Version of MongoDB that the cluster runs. |

When configured as `NODE_TYPE`, Atlas scales your electable nodes in parallel with your read-only and a |

### validateGroupClusterConfigurations

`clusters.validateGroupClusterConfigurations`

Validate One Cluster Configuration: checks if the given cluster configuration is valid and ready to be used to create or edit a cluster

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.clusters.validateGroupClusterConfigurations({
	groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718',
	clusterDescription: {},
	editing: true,
});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `useEffectiveInstanceFields` | `boolean` | No | When true, hardware specification fields for autoscaling-enabled clusters are resolved to their effective (current operational) values before validating an edit. When false (default), the client-specified values are validated. Set this to match the header sent on the corresponding cluster update. |
| `useEffectiveFieldsReplicationSpecs` | `boolean` | No | Controls how `replicationSpecs` are interpreted for auto-sharded clusters when validating an edit. When false (default), `replicationSpecs` is treated as the actual cluster state. |
| `advancedConfiguration` | `object` | No | Advanced MongoDB process configuration options applied to the cluster. |
| `clusterDescription` | `object` | Yes | Configuration of a MongoDB Atlas cluster, including its replication topology, instance sizing, storage, and operational settings. |
| `clusterName` | `string` | No | Name of the existing cluster to validate against when editing is true. |
| `editing` | `boolean` | Yes | When true, validates the configuration as an update to an existing cluster. When false, validates as a new cluster create. |
| `searchDeploymentSpec` | `object` | No | Hardware specification for the Search Nodes that back a search deployment. |
| `tags` | `object[]` | No | Optional list of resource tags. |

## Collection Level Metrics

### getClusterNamespaces

`collectionLevelMetrics.getClusterNamespaces`

Return Ranked Namespaces from One Cluster: return the subset of namespaces from the given cluster sorted by highest total execution time (descending) within the given time window

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.collectionLevelMetrics.getClusterNamespaces({ groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718', clusterName: 'Cluster0', clusterView: 'PRIMARY' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `clusterName` | `string` | Yes | Human-readable label that identifies the cluster to pin namespaces to. |
| `clusterView` | `PRIMARY \| SECONDARY \| INDIVIDUAL_PROCESS` | Yes | Human-readable label that identifies the cluster topology to retrieve metrics for. |
| `start` | `string` | No | Date and time when MongoDB Cloud begins reporting the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **period**. |
| `end` | `string` | No | Date and time when MongoDB Cloud stops reporting the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **period**. |
| `period` | `string` | No | Duration over which Atlas reports the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 duration format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **start** and **end**. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string \| null` | No | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the request project. |
| `identifierId` | `string \| null` | No | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the request process. |
| `rankedNamespaces` | `string[] \| null` | No | Ordered list of the hottest namespaces, highest value first. |



---

### getProcessNamespaces

`collectionLevelMetrics.getProcessNamespaces`

Return Ranked Namespaces from One Host: return the subset of namespaces from the given process ranked by highest total execution time (descending) within the given time window

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.collectionLevelMetrics.getProcessNamespaces({ groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718', processId: 'cluster0-shard-00-00.abcde.mongodb.net:27017' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `processId` | `string` | Yes | Combination of hostname and IANA port that serves the MongoDB process. The host must be the hostname, fully qualified domain name (FQDN), or Internet Protocol address (IPv4 or IPv6) of the host that runs the MongoDB process (mongod or mongos). The port must be the IANA port on which the MongoDB process listens for requests. |
| `start` | `string` | No | Date and time when MongoDB Cloud begins reporting the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **period**. |
| `end` | `string` | No | Date and time when MongoDB Cloud stops reporting the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **period**. |
| `period` | `string` | No | Duration over which Atlas reports the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 duration format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **start** and **end**. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string \| null` | No | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the request project. |
| `identifierId` | `string \| null` | No | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the request process. |
| `rankedNamespaces` | `string[] \| null` | No | Ordered list of the hottest namespaces, highest value first. |

### listCollStatMeasurements

`collectionLevelMetrics.listCollStatMeasurements`

Return Cluster-Level Query Latency: get a list of the Coll Stats Latency cluster-level measurements for the given namespace

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.collectionLevelMetrics.listCollStatMeasurements({
	groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718',
	clusterName: 'Cluster0',
	clusterView: 'PRIMARY',
	databaseName: 'sample_mflix',
	collectionName: 'movies',
});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `clusterName` | `string` | Yes | Human-readable label that identifies the cluster to retrieve metrics for. |
| `clusterView` | `PRIMARY \| SECONDARY \| INDIVIDUAL_PROCESS` | Yes | Human-readable label that identifies the cluster topology to retrieve metrics for. |

## Database Users

### createDatabaseUser

`databaseUsers.createDatabaseUser`

Create One Database User in One Project: creates one database user in the specified project

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.databaseUsers.createDatabaseUser({
	groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718',
	databaseName: 'admin',
	username: 'app-user',
	password: 'correct-horse-battery-staple',
	roles: [{ databaseName: 'sample_mflix', roleName: 'readWrite' }],
});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `awsIAMType` | `NONE \| USER \| ROLE` | No | Human-readable label that indicates whether the new database user authenticates with the Amazon Web Services (AWS) Identity and Access Management (IAM) credentials associated with the user or the user's role. |
| `databaseName` | `admin \| $external` | Yes | The database against which the database user authenticates. Database users must provide both a username and authentication database to log into MongoDB. If the user authenticates with AWS IAM, x.509, LDAP, or OIDC Workload this value should be `$external`. If the user authenticates with SCRAM-SHA or OIDC Workforce, this value should be `admin`. |
| `deleteAfterDate` | `string` | No | Date and time when MongoDB Cloud deletes the user. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC and can include the time zone designation. You must specify a future date that falls within one week of making the Application Programming Interface (API) request. |
| `description` | `string` | No | Description of this database user. |
| `labels` | `object[]` | No | List that contains the key-value pairs for tagging and categorizing the MongoDB database user. The labels that you define do not appear in the console. |
| `ldapAuthType` | `NONE \| GROUP \| USER` | No | Part of the Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) record that the database uses to authenticate this database user on the LDAP host. |
| `oidcAuthType` | `NONE \| IDP_GROUP \| USER` | No | Human-readable label that indicates whether the new database user or group authenticates with OIDC federated authentication. To create a federated authentication user, specify the value of USER in this field. To create a federated authentication group, specify the value of `IDP_GROUP` in this field. |
| `password` | `string` | No | Alphanumeric string that authenticates this database user against the database specified in `databaseName`. To authenticate with SCRAM-SHA, you must specify this parameter. This parameter doesn't appear in this response. |
| `roles` | `object[]` | Yes | List that provides the pairings of one role with one applicable database. |
| `scopes` | `object[]` | No | List that contains clusters, MongoDB Atlas Data Lakes, and MongoDB Atlas Streams Workspaces that this database user can access. If omitted, MongoDB Cloud grants the database user access to all the clusters, MongoDB Atlas Data Lakes, and MongoDB Atlas Streams Workspaces in the project. |
| `username` | `string` | Yes | Human-readable label that represents the user that authenticates to MongoDB. The format of this label depends on the method of authentication: \| Authentication Method \| Parameter Needed \| Parameter Value \| username Format \| \|---\|---\|---\|---\| \| AWS IAM \| `awsIAMType` \| `ROLE` \| &lt;abbr title="Amazon Resource Name"&gt;ARN&lt;/abbr&gt; \| \| AWS IAM \| `awsIAMType` \| `USER` \| &lt;abbr title="Amazon Resource Name"&gt;ARN&lt;/abbr&gt; \| \| x.509 \| `x509Type` \| `CUSTOMER` \| [RFC 2253](https://tools.ietf.org/html/2253) Distingui |
| `x509Type` | `NONE \| CUSTOMER \| MANAGED` | No | X.509 method that MongoDB Cloud uses to authenticate the database user. - For application-managed X.509, specify `MANAGED`. - For self-managed X.509, specify `CUSTOMER`. Users created with the `CUSTOMER` method require a Common Name (CN) in the **username** parameter. You must create externally authenticated users on the `$external` database. |

## Data Federation

### createDataFederation

`dataFederation.createDataFederation`

Create One Federated Database Instance in One Project: creates one federated database instance in the specified project

**Risk:** `destructive`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.dataFederation.createDataFederation({ groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `skipRoleValidation` | `boolean` | No | Flag that indicates whether this request should check if the requesting IAM role can read from the S3 bucket. AWS checks if the role can list the objects in the bucket before writing to it. Some IAM roles only need write permissions. This flag allows you to skip that check. |
| `cloudProviderConfig` | `object` | No | Cloud provider where this Federated Database Instance is hosted. |
| `dataProcessRegion` | `object` | No | Information about the cloud provider region to which the Federated Database Instance routes client connections. |
| `name` | `string` | No | Human-readable label that identifies the Federated Database Instance. |
| `storage` | `object` | No | Configuration information for each data store and its mapping to MongoDB Cloud databases. |

### createPrivateEndpointId

`dataFederation.createPrivateEndpointId`

Create One Federated Database Instance and Online Archive Private Endpoint for One Project: adds one private endpoint for Federated Database Instances and Online Archives to the specified projects

**Risk:** `destructive`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.dataFederation.createPrivateEndpointId({ groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718', endpointId: 'vpce-0123456789abcdef0' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `azureLinkId` | `string` | No | Link ID that identifies the Azure private endpoint connection. |
| `comment` | `string` | No | Human-readable string to associate with this private endpoint. |
| `customerEndpointDNSName` | `string` | No | Human-readable label to identify customer's VPC endpoint DNS name. If defined, you must also specify a value for `region`. |
| `customerEndpointIPAddress` | `string` | No | IP address used to connect to the Azure private endpoint. |
| `endpointId` | `string` | Yes | Unique string that identifies the private endpoint. For AWS, this is a 22-character alphanumeric string in the format `vpce-<17 hex characters>`. For Azure, this is the full resource ID in the format `/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/resourceGroups/{resourceGroupName}/providers/Microsoft.Network/privateEndpoints/{endpointName}`. |
| `errorMessage` | `string` | No | Error message describing a failure approving the private endpoint request. |
| `provider` | `AWS \| AZURE` | No | Human-readable label that identifies the cloud service provider. Atlas Data Lake supports Amazon Web Services and Azure. |
| `region` | `string` | No | Human-readable label to identify the region of customer's VPC endpoint. If defined, you must also specify a value for `customerEndpointDNSName`. |
| `status` | `PENDING \| OK \| FAILED \| DELETING` | No | Status of the private endpoint connection request. |
| `type` | `DATA_LAKE` | No | Human-readable label that identifies the resource type associated with this private endpoint. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `links` | `object[] \| null` | No | List of one or more Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) that point to API sub-resources, related API resources, or both. RFC 5988 outlines these relationships. |
| `results` | `object[] \| null` | No | List of returned documents that MongoDB Cloud provides when completing this request. |
| `totalCount` | `number \| null` | No | Total number of documents available. When `includeCount` is set to `false`, MongoDB Cloud may omit this value or return it when the count is available without additional calculation. The total number is an estimate and may not be exact. |

### deleteDataFederation

`dataFederation.deleteDataFederation`

Remove One Federated Database Instance from One Project: removes one federated database instance from the specified project

**Risk:** `destructive` · **Irreversible**

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.dataFederation.deleteDataFederation({ groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718', tenantName: 'example-tenant' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `tenantName` | `string` | Yes | Human-readable label that identifies the federated database instance to remove. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `success` | `true` | Yes | MongoDBAtlas accepted the call; it answered with no body (or an empty object). |

| `limitName` | `bytesProcessed.query \| bytesProcessed.daily \| bytesProcessed.weekly \| bytesProcessed.monthly` | Yes | Human-readable label that identifies this data federation instance limit. \| Limit Name \| Description \| Default \| \| --- \| --- \| --- \| \| `bytesProcessed.query` \| Limit on the number of bytes processed during a single data federation query \| N/A \| \| `bytesProcessed.daily` \| Limit on the number of bytes processed for the data federation instance for the current day \| N/A \| \| `bytesProcessed.weekly` \| Limit on the number of bytes processed for the data federation instance for the current week \| N/A \| |

### downloadFederationQueryLogs

`dataFederation.downloadFederationQueryLogs`

Download Query Logs for One Federated Database Instance: downloads the query logs for the specified federated database instance (returned as a file)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.dataFederation.downloadFederationQueryLogs({ groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718', tenantName: 'example-tenant' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `endDate` | `number` | No | Timestamp that specifies the end point for the range of log messages to download. MongoDB Cloud expresses this timestamp in the number of seconds that have elapsed since the UNIX epoch. |
| `startDate` | `number` | No | Timestamp that specifies the starting point for the range of log messages to download. MongoDB Cloud expresses this timestamp in the number of seconds that have elapsed since the UNIX epoch. |
| `tenantName` | `string` | Yes | Human-readable label that identifies the federated database instance for which you want to download query logs. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `contentBase64` | `string` | No | The file, base64-encoded. Missing when the file came back as text or contentOmitted is set. |
| `text` | `string` | No | The file as text, in place of contentBase64, when it is a text file (CSV, JSON, Markdown, XML and the like) in UTF-8. |
| `contentType` | `string` | Yes | Media type of the file, for example application/pdf. |
| `byteLength` | `number` | Yes | Size of the file in bytes. |
| `filename` | `string` | No | The file name, when known. |
| `contentOmitted` | `not_requested \| over_limit` | No | Set when the content was left out: the caller did not ask for it, or the file was over the limit. |
| `fileId` | `string` | No | Where the host saved the file. Over the limit it comes in place of the content; a host that keeps every file sets it beside the content too. On Corsair it is a Files id (fil_…): pass it to another app wherever that app takes a file URL, or read a text file or PDF with files.read_text. |

---

### getOrgEvent

`events.getOrgEvent`

Return One Event from One Organization: returns one event for the specified organization

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.events.getOrgEvent({ orgId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718', eventId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `orgId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the organization that contains your projects. Use the [`/orgs`](#tag/Organizations/operation/listOrganizations) endpoint to retrieve all organizations to which the authenticated user has access. |
| `eventId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the event that you want to return. |
| `includeRaw` | `boolean` | No | Flag that indicates whether to include the raw document in the output. The raw document contains additional meta information about the event. |



**Output:** `object`

### listEventTypes

`events.listEventTypes`

Return All Event Types: returns a list of all event types, along with a description and additional metadata about each event (paged with pageNum / itemsPerPage)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.events.listEventTypes({});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `includeCount` | `boolean` | No | Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud calculates the total number of items for the response. When set to `false`, MongoDB Cloud may skip an additional count operation. The response may still include `totalCount` when the count is available without additional calculation. |
| `itemsPerPage` | `number` | No | Number of items that the response returns per page. |
| `pageNum` | `number` | No | Number of the page that displays the current set of the total objects that the response returns. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `links` | `object[] \| null` | No | List of one or more Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) that point to API sub-resources, related API resources, or both. RFC 5988 outlines these relationships. |
| `results` | `object[] \| null` | No | List of returned documents that MongoDB Cloud provides when completing this request. |
| `totalCount` | `number \| null` | No | Total number of documents available. When `includeCount` is set to `false`, MongoDB Cloud may omit this value or return it when the count is available without additional calculation. The total number is an estimate and may not be exact. |

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="links full type">

```ts
{
  href?: string | null,
  rel?: string | null
}[] | null
```
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="results full type">

```ts
{
  alertable?: boolean | null,
  description?: string | null,
  eventType?: string | null
}[] | null
```
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

### listGroupEvents

`events.listGroupEvents`

Return Events from One Project: returns events for the specified project (paged with pageNum / itemsPerPage)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.events.listGroupEvents({ groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |

change frequently. Verify that you specify the event type correctly by checking the complete list of event types. |
| `includeRaw` | `boolean` | No | Flag that indicates whether to include the raw document in the output. The raw document contains additional meta information about the event. |
| `maxDate` | `string` | No | Date and time from when MongoDB Cloud stops returning events. This parameter uses the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. |
| `minDate` | `string` | No | Date and time from when MongoDB Cloud starts returning events. This parameter uses the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `links` | `object[] \| null` | No | List of one or more Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) that point to API sub-resources, related API resources, or both. RFC 5988 outlines these relationships. |
| `results` | `object[] \| null` | No | List of returned documents that MongoDB Cloud provides when completing this request. |
| `totalCount` | `number \| null` | No | Total number of documents available. When `includeCount` is set to `false`, MongoDB Cloud may omit this value or return it when the count is available without additional calculation. The total number is an estimate and may not be exact. |
