### listQueryShapeSummaries

`queryShapeInsights.listQueryShapeSummaries`

Return Query Statistic Summaries: returns a list of query shape statistics summaries for a given cluster

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.queryShapeInsights.listQueryShapeSummaries({ groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718', clusterName: 'Cluster0' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `clusterName` | `string` | Yes | Human-readable label that identifies the cluster. |
| `since` | `number` | No | Date and time from which to retrieve query shape statistics. This parameter expresses its value in the number of milliseconds that have elapsed since the [UNIX epoch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time). - If you don't specify the **until** parameter, the endpoint returns data covering from the **since** value and the current time. - If you specify neither the **since** nor the **until** parameters, the endpoint returns data from the previous 24 hours. |
| `until` | `number` | No | Date and time up until which to retrieve query shape statistics. This parameter expresses its value in the number of milliseconds that have elapsed since the [UNIX epoch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time). - If you specify the **until** parameter, you must specify the **since** parameter. - If you specify neither the **since** nor the **until** parameters, the endpoint returns data from the previous 24 hours. |
| `processIds` | `string[]` | No | Process IDs from which to retrieve query shape statistics. A `processId` is a combination of host and port that serves the MongoDB process. The host must be the hostname, FQDN, IPv4 address, or IPv6 address of the host that runs the MongoDB process (`mongod` or `mongos`). The port must be the IANA port on which the MongoDB process listens for requests. To include multiple `processId`, pass the parameter multiple times delimited with an ampersand (`&`) between each `processId`. |
| `namespaces` | `string[]` | No | Namespaces from which to retrieve query shape statistics. A namespace consists of one database and one collection resource written as `.`: `<database>.<collection>`. To include multiple namespaces, pass the parameter multiple times delimited with an ampersand (`&`) between each namespace. Omit this parameter to return results for all namespaces. |
| `commands` | `(find \| distinct \| aggregate \| count \| insert \| update \| delete)[]` | No | Retrieve query shape statistics matching specified MongoDB commands. To include multiple commands, pass the parameter multiple times delimited with an ampersand (`&`) between each command. The currently supported parameters are: find, distinct, aggregate, count, insert, update, and delete. The insert, update, and delete commands return results only for clusters running MongoDB 9.0 or later with write query shape statistics enabled for the project. Omit this parameter to return results for all su |
| `nSummaries` | `number` | No | Maximum number of query statistic summaries to return. |
| `series` | `(TOTAL_EXECUTION_TIME \| AVG_EXECUTION_TIME \| EXECUTION_COUNT \| KEYS_EXAMINED \| DOCS_EXAMINED \| DOCS_RETURNED \| TOTAL_TIME_TO_RESPONSE \| AVG_TIME_TO_RESPONSE \| BYTES_READ \| CPU_TIME \| KEYS_EXAMINED_RETURNED \| DOCS_EXAMINED_RETURNED \| LAST_EXECUTION_TIME \| P50_EXECUTION_TIME \| P90_EXECUTION_TIME \| P99_EXECUTION_TIME \| DOCS_MATCHED \| DOCS_MODIFIED \| DOCS_UPSERTED \| DOCS_DELETED \| DOCS_INSERTED \| KEYS_INSERTED \| KEYS_DELETED)[]` | No | Query shape statistics data series to retrieve. A series represents a specific metric about query execution. To include multiple series, pass the parameter multiple times delimited with an ampersand (`&`) between each series. Omit this parameter to return results for all available series. The `P50_EXECUTION_TIME`, `P90_EXECUTION_TIME`, and `P99_EXECUTION_TIME` series are deprecated as the values they report may be inaccurate. They will be removed in a future release. |
| `queryShapeHashes` | `string[]` | No | A list of SHA256 hashes of desired query shapes, output by MongoDB commands like `$queryStats` and $explain or slow query logs. To include multiple series, pass the parameter multiple times delimited with an ampersand (`&`) between each series. Omit this parameter to return results for all available series. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `message` | `string \| null` | No | Explanation of query shape insights availability limitations on the current tier. |
| `queryStatsCollection` | `object \| null` | No | How `queryStats` entries were collected on this cluster's processes. Reflects the collection mode of the cluster's processes regardless of any host or process type filters in the request. Omitted when the collection mode cannot be determined. Sample-based collection requires MongoDB 9.0 or later but may not be enabled on every such cluster; this reflects the mode in effect on the cluster. |
| `scale` | `object \| null` | No | Information on scaling the cluster to a tier that supports the requested feature. Present only when the feature is unavailable on the cluster's current tier. |
| `summaries` | `object[] \| null` | No | List of query shape statistic summaries from Query Shape Insights. |

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.queryShapeInsights.updateClusterQueryShape({
	groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718',
	clusterName: 'Cluster0',
	queryShapeHash: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f607185f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f607185f43e7f0a1b2c3d4',
	status: 'REJECTED',
});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `clusterName` | `string` | Yes | Human-readable label that identifies the cluster. |
| `queryShapeHash` | `string` | Yes | A SHA256 hash of a query shape, output by MongoDB commands like `$queryStats` and `$explain` or slow query logs. |
| `status` | `REJECTED \| UNREJECTED` | Yes | The rejection status of a query shape. Use REJECTED to prevent the query shape from executing on the cluster, or UNREJECTED to allow it to execute. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `command` | `string \| null` | No | The MongoDB command type issued for a query shape. The INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE commands appear only for clusters running MongoDB 9.0 or later. |
| `namespace` | `string \| null` | No | Human-readable label that identifies the namespace on the specified host. The resource expresses this parameter value as `<database>.<collection>`. |
| `queryShape` | `string \| null` | No | A query shape is a set of specifications that group similar queries together. Specifications can include filters, sorts, projections, aggregation pipeline stages, a namespace, and others. Queries that have similar specifications have the same query shape. This field may be null if the user lacks PII view access. |
| `queryShapeHash` | `string \| null` | No | A hexadecimal string that represents the hash of a MongoDB query shape. |
| `status` | `string \| null` | No | The rejection status of a query shape. Use REJECTED to prevent the query shape from executing on the cluster, or UNREJECTED to allow it to execute. |

`rateLimiting.getRateLimit`

Return One Rate Limit: get one rate limit endpoint set

**Risk:** `read`


**Input**

| `groupId` | `string` | No | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the Atlas Project to request rate limits for. When this parameter is provided, the limits returned are applicable to the specified project. The requesting user must have the Project Read Only role for the specified project. |
| `orgId` | `string` | No | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the Atlas Organization to request rate limits for. When this parameter is provided, the limits returned are applicable to the specified organization. The requesting user must have the Organization Read Only role for the specified organization. |

When this parameter is provided, the limits returned are applicable to the specified user. The requesting user must be the same as the specified user. |

## Rolling Index

### createRollingIndex

`rollingIndex.createRollingIndex`

Create One Rolling Index: creates an index on the cluster identified by its name in a rolling manner

**Risk:** `destructive`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.rollingIndex.createRollingIndex({
	groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718',
	clusterName: 'Cluster0',
	collection: 'example',
	db: 'example',
	keys: [{}],
});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `clusterName` | `string` | Yes | Human-readable label that identifies the cluster on which MongoDB Cloud creates an index. |
| `collation` | `object` | No | One or more settings that specify language-specific rules to compare strings within this index. |
| `collection` | `string` | Yes | Human-readable label of the collection for which MongoDB Cloud creates an index. |
| `db` | `string` | Yes | Human-readable label of the database that holds the collection on which MongoDB Cloud creates an index. |
| `keys` | `Record<string, string>[]` | Yes | List that contains one or more objects that describe the parameters that you want to index. |
| `options` | `object` | No | One or more settings that determine how the MongoDB Cloud creates this MongoDB index. |

```ts
  alternate?: non-ignorable | shifted,
```

### createGroupSecret

`serviceAccounts.createGroupSecret`

Create One Project Service Account Secret: create a secret for the specified Service Account in the specified Project

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.serviceAccounts.createGroupSecret({ groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718', clientId: 'mdb_sa_id_5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718', secretExpiresAfterHours: 1 });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `clientId` | `string` | Yes | The Client ID of the Service Account. |
| `secretExpiresAfterHours` | `number` | Yes | The expiration time of the new Service Account secret, provided in hours. The minimum and maximum allowed expiration times are subject to change and are controlled by the organization's settings. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `createdAt` | `string \| null` | No | The date that the secret was created on. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. |
| `expiresAt` | `string \| null` | No | The date for the expiration of the secret. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. |
| `id` | `string \| null` | No | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the secret. |
| `lastUsedAt` | `string \| null \| null` | No | The last time the secret was used. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. |
| `maskedSecretValue` | `string \| null` | No | The masked Service Account secret. |
| `secret` | `string \| null` | No | The secret for the Service Account. It will be returned only the first time after creation. |

### createGroupServiceAccount

`serviceAccounts.createGroupServiceAccount`

Create One Project Service Account: creates one Service Account for the specified Project

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.serviceAccounts.createGroupServiceAccount({
	groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718',
	description: 'example',
	name: 'Cluster0',
	roles: ['example'],
});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `description` | `string` | Yes | Human readable description for the Service Account. |
| `name` | `string` | Yes | Human-readable name for the Service Account. The name is modifiable and does not have to be unique. |
| `roles` | `string[]` | Yes | A list of project-level roles for the Service Account. |
| `secretExpiresAfterHours` | `number \| null` | No | The expiration time of the new Service Account secret, provided in hours. The minimum and maximum allowed expiration times are subject to change and are controlled by the organization's settings. Required unless `withoutInitialSecret` is true. |
| `withoutInitialSecret` | `boolean` | No | If true, creates the Service Account without generating an initial secret. `secretExpiresAfterHours` must not be set when this is true. Defaults to false, which preserves existing behavior: a secret is generated and returned in the response. Use the `CreateGroupServiceAccountSecret` endpoint to add a secret later. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `clientId` | `string \| null` | No | The Client ID of the Service Account. |
| `createdAt` | `string \| null` | No | The date that the Service Account was created on. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. |
| `description` | `string \| null` | No | Human readable description for the Service Account. |
| `name` | `string \| null` | No | Human-readable name for the Service Account. |
| `roles` | `string[] \| null` | No | A list of Project roles associated with the Service Account. |
| `secrets` | `object[] \| null` | No | A list of secrets associated with the specified Service Account. |
| `systemManaged` | `boolean \| null` | No | Indicates whether the Service Account is system managed. |

```ts
}[] | null
```

## Sharding Insights

### getClusterShardingInsights

`shardingInsights.getClusterShardingInsights`

Return Sharding Insights for One Cluster: returns the cluster-level sharding state of one sharded cluster: the number of shards, the balancer state, the availability of the config servers, and the configured balancing window

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.shardingInsights.getClusterShardingInsights({ groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718', clusterName: 'Cluster0' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `clusterName` | `string` | Yes | Human-readable label that identifies the cluster. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `balancerState` | `string \| null` | No | State of the cluster balancer. `BALANCING` means a balancer round is in progress. `IDLE` means the balancer is enabled and no round is in progress. `DISABLED` means the balancer is turned off. `FAILED_TO_DETERMINE` means the balancer state could not be resolved. |
| `balancingWindow` | `object \| null` | No | Balancing window configured on the sharded cluster. When configured, the balancer moves data only during the daily interval between `startTime` and `endTime`. |
| `configServerStatus` | `string \| null` | No | Availability of the cluster's config servers. `AVAILABLE` means at least one config server reported recently. `UNAVAILABLE` means config servers exist but none has reported recently. `FAILED_TO_DETERMINE` means availability could not be resolved. |
| `totalShards` | `number \| null` | No | Number of shards in the cluster. |

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="balancingWindow full type">

```ts
{
  endTime?: string | null | null,
  startTime?: string | null | null,
  status?: string | null
} | null
```
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

### getClusterShardMetric

`shardingInsights.getClusterShardMetric`

Return One Shard in One Cluster: returns the size, load and open alerts of one shard in one sharded cluster

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.shardingInsights.getClusterShardMetric({ groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718', clusterName: 'Cluster0', replicaSetName: 'example' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `clusterName` | `string` | Yes | Human-readable label that identifies the cluster. |
| `replicaSetName` | `string` | Yes | Name of the replica set that identifies the shard. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `alerts` | `object[] \| null` | No | Alerts open on this shard's nodes, sorted by creation date with the most recently created first. MongoDB Cloud returns this property when you request a single shard, and returns at most 100 alerts. |
| `cacheThroughput` | `object \| null` | No | Bytes per second that the shard moved in and out of the cache over the last hour. |
| `cpuUtilization` | `object \| null` | No | CPU utilization of the shard's nodes over the last hour, as a percentage. |
| `dataSizeBytes` | `number \| null` | No | Total size of the user data stored on this shard. The resource expresses this value in bytes. |
| `rangeDeleterTasks` | `number \| null` | No | Average number of range deletion tasks queued across the shard's nodes, measured at the time of the request. |
| `readLatencyMicroseconds` | `number \| null` | No | Average latency of the read operations this shard served over the last hour, in microseconds. |
| `readOperationsPerSecond` | `object \| null` | No | Operations per second that the shard served over the last hour. |
| `replicaSetName` | `string \| null` | No | Name of the shard's replica set. This is the name that identifies the same shard on the processes, alerts, events, and backup resources. |
| `shardedCollections` | `number \| null` | No | Number of sharded collections with data on this shard. |
| `warnings` | `string[] \| null` | No | Conditions that MongoDB Cloud observed on this shard relative to the rest of the cluster. `HOTSPOT` means this shard's average CPU utilization is more than twice the average across all shards of the cluster. This is a cluster-scoped comparison, so its value depends on how loaded the other shards are and not only on this shard. |
| `writeOperationsPerSecond` | `object \| null` | No | Operations per second that the shard served over the last hour. |

## Shard Key Analyzer

### createShardKeyAnalysis

`shardKeyAnalyzer.createShardKeyAnalysis`

Create One Shard Key Analysis for One Cluster: analyzes how well one candidate shard key would distribute one collection across the shards of the specified cluster

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.shardKeyAnalyzer.createShardKeyAnalysis({
	groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718',
	clusterName: 'Cluster0',
	namespace: 'example',
	shardKey: [{}],
});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `clusterName` | `string` | Yes | Human-readable label that identifies the cluster that contains the collection to analyze. |
| `includeKeyCharacteristics` | `boolean` | No | Flag that indicates whether to return the cardinality, frequency and monotonicity of the candidate shard key. |
| `includeReadWriteDistribution` | `boolean` | No | Flag that indicates whether to return how reads and writes would be routed across shards under the candidate shard key. This requires query sampling to have collected operations for the namespace. |
| `namespace` | `string` | Yes | Combination of the database and collection to analyze, written as `<database>.<collection>`. |
| `shardKey` | `Record<string, string>[]` | Yes | Candidate shard key, given as one object per shard key field in the order the fields form the key. Field order is significant: `[{"a": "1"}, {"b": "1"}]` and `[{"b": "1"}, {"a": "1"}]` are different shard keys. At most one field may be `hashed`. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `success` | `true` | Yes | MongoDBAtlas accepted the call; it answered with no body (or an empty object). |

### getAnalysisOperation

`shardKeyAnalyzer.getAnalysisOperation`

Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |

**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |

| `createdAt` | `string \| null` | No | Date and time when MongoDB Cloud accepted this operation (ISO 8601 format in UTC). |

| `expiresAt` | `string \| null` | No | Date and time when MongoDB Cloud stops returning this operation (ISO 8601 format in UTC). Reads after this time return an HTTP 404 status. This value derives from `updatedAt`, so it advances with each state change while the operation is running and settles only once the operation is terminal. |
| `operationId` | `string \| null` | No | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies this operation. When the operation succeeds, the analysis it created carries the same identifier. |
| `operationType` | `string \| null` | No | Kind of change the operation makes. Submitting a shard key analysis creates an analysis resource, so the operation type is always `CREATE`. |
| `resultHref` | `string \| null` | No | URI of the analysis this operation created. MongoDB Cloud returns this parameter only when `status` is `SUCCEEDED`. |
| `retryAfterSeconds` | `number \| null` | No | Number of seconds to wait before polling this operation again. MongoDB Cloud returns this parameter only while `status` is not terminal. |
| `status` | `string \| null` | No | State of the shard key analysis operation. `PENDING` and `IN_PROGRESS` are non-terminal; `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELED` and `SUPERSEDED` are terminal. MongoDB Cloud currently reports only `PENDING`, `SUCCEEDED` and `FAILED`. The remaining values are reserved and may be reported in the future without a new resource version. |
| `updatedAt` | `string \| null` | No | Date and time when this operation last changed state (ISO 8601 format in UTC). Once the operation is terminal, this is when it finished. |

### getShardKeyAnalysis

`shardKeyAnalyzer.getShardKeyAnalysis`

Return One Shard Key Analysis for One Cluster: returns one completed shard key analysis for the specified cluster

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.shardKeyAnalyzer.getShardKeyAnalysis({ groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718', clusterName: 'Cluster0', analysisId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `clusterName` | `string` | Yes | Human-readable label that identifies the cluster with the shard key analysis you want to return. |
| `analysisId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the shard key analysis to return. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `avgDocSizeBytes` | `number \| null` | No | Average size of one document in the collection, in bytes. |
| `correlationCoefficient` | `number \| null` | No | Correlation between the candidate shard key and the order in which documents were inserted, from `-1` to `1`. Values near `1` or `-1` indicate a monotonically changing key, which directs all inserts to one shard. This parameter is absent when the shard key has no supporting index or the collection is clustered, in which case MongoDB Cloud does not compute it. |
| `createdAt` | `string \| null` | No | Date and time when this shard key analysis was requested (ISO 8601 format in UTC). This is when the analysis was submitted, not when it completed; the completion time is the `updatedAt` of the operation that produced it. |
| `expiresAt` | `string \| null` | No | Date and time when MongoDB Cloud stops returning this shard key analysis (ISO 8601 format in UTC). Reads after this time return an HTTP 404 status. |
| `id` | `string \| null` | No | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies this shard key analysis. This is the same identifier as the `operationId` of the operation that produced it. |
| `isUnique` | `boolean \| null` | No | Flag that indicates whether the index supporting the candidate shard key enforces a uniqueness constraint. |
| `monotonicity` | `string \| null` | No | Whether the shard key value increases or decreases with the order in which documents were inserted. A monotonically changing shard key directs all inserts to one shard. `UNKNOWN` indicates that MongoDB Cloud could not determine monotonicity, which happens when the shard key has no supporting index or the collection is clustered. |
| `mostCommonValues` | `object[] \| null` | No | Shard key values that occur most frequently in the sampled documents, with how often each occurs. MongoDB Cloud returns this parameter only to callers that can read the collection's data, because it carries values out of the collection rather than statistics about them. |
| `namespace` | `string \| null` | No | Combination of the database and collection that was analyzed, written as `<database>.<collection>`. |
| `note` | `string \| null` | No | Guidance from MongoDB on how to interpret the metrics in this analysis. This parameter is absent when the analysis carries no guidance. |
| `numDistinctValues` | `number \| null` | No | Number of distinct values that the candidate shard key takes across the sampled documents. A value close to `numDocsSampled` indicates high cardinality, which distributes documents well. |
| `numDocsSampled` | `number \| null` | No | Number of documents that MongoDB Cloud sampled to compute these metrics. |
| `numDocsTotal` | `number \| null` | No | Number of documents in the collection. |
| `numOrphanDocs` | `number \| null` | No | Number of orphaned documents in the collection. This parameter is absent for collections that have none. |
| `percentageOfMultiShardReads` | `number \| null` | No | Percentage of sampled reads that the candidate shard key would route to more than one shard but not to every shard. |
| `percentageOfMultiShardWrites` | `number \| null` | No | Percentage of sampled writes that the candidate shard key would route to more than one shard but not to every shard. |
| `percentageOfScatterGatherReads` | `number \| null` | No | Percentage of sampled reads that the candidate shard key would broadcast to every shard. Lower is better. |
| `percentageOfScatterGatherWrites` | `number \| null` | No | Percentage of sampled writes that the candidate shard key would broadcast to every shard. Lower is better. |
| `percentageOfSingleShardReads` | `number \| null` | No | Percentage of sampled reads that the candidate shard key would route to exactly one shard. Higher is better. |
| `percentageOfSingleShardWrites` | `number \| null` | No | Percentage of sampled writes that the candidate shard key would route to exactly one shard. Higher is better. |
| `rawOutput` | `string \| null` | No | Unmodified result of the `analyzeShardKey` command, as a JSON string. Its content tracks the MongoDB server version of the analyzed cluster rather than the version of this resource, so members outside the parameters above may appear or change without a new resource version. Do not parse it as a stable contract. `mostCommonValues` is removed from it for callers that cannot read the collection's data. This parameter is absent if MongoDB Cloud could not serialize the command result, which costs the |
| `readSampleSize` | `object \| null` | No | Number of sampled read operations that MongoDB Cloud used to compute the read distribution, broken down by the command that issued them. |
| `shardKey` | `Record<string, string>[] \| null` | No | Candidate shard key that was analyzed, given as one object per shard key field in the order the fields form the key. This parameter is absent when MongoDB Cloud has no shard key recorded for the analysis. |
| `writeSampleSize` | `object \| null` | No | Number of sampled write operations that MongoDB Cloud used to compute the write distribution, broken down by the command that issued them. |

### downloadAuditLogs

`streams.downloadAuditLogs`

Download Audit Logs for One Atlas Stream Processing Workspace: downloads the audit logs for the specified Atlas Streams Processing workspace or stream processor (returned as a file)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.streams.downloadAuditLogs({ groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718', tenantName: 'example-tenant' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `endDate` | `number` | No | Timestamp that specifies the end point for the range of log messages to download. MongoDB Cloud expresses this timestamp in the number of seconds that have elapsed since the UNIX epoch. |
| `startDate` | `number` | No | Timestamp that specifies the starting point for the range of log messages to download. MongoDB Cloud expresses this timestamp in the number of seconds that have elapsed since the UNIX epoch. |
| `spName` | `string` | No | Name of the stream processor to download logs for. An empty string will download logs for all stream processors in the workspace. |
| `tenantName` | `string` | Yes | Label that identifies the stream workspace. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `contentBase64` | `string` | No | The file, base64-encoded. Missing when the file came back as text or contentOmitted is set. |
| `text` | `string` | No | The file as text, in place of contentBase64, when it is a text file (CSV, JSON, Markdown, XML and the like) in UTF-8. |
| `contentType` | `string` | Yes | Media type of the file, for example application/pdf. |
| `byteLength` | `number` | Yes | Size of the file in bytes. |
| `filename` | `string` | No | The file name, when known. |
| `contentOmitted` | `not_requested \| over_limit` | No | Set when the content was left out: the caller did not ask for it, or the file was over the limit. |
| `fileId` | `string` | No | Where the host saved the file. Over the limit it comes in place of the content; a host that keeps every file sets it beside the content too. On Corsair it is a Files id (fil_…): pass it to another app wherever that app takes a file URL, or read a text file or PDF with files.read_text. |

| `gcpConnectionIds` | `string[] \| null` | No | List of GCP Private Service Connect connection IDs. |

| `provider` | `string \| null` | No | Cloud provider where the private endpoint's target resource is deployed. Valid values are AWS, AZURE, and GCP. |
| `providerAccountId` | `string \| null` | No | Account ID from the cloud provider. |
| `region` | `string \| null` | No | The region of the Provider’s cluster. See [AWS](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/amazon-aws/#stream-processing-workspaces), [AZURE](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/microsoft-azure/#stream-processing-workspaces), and [GCP](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/google-gcp/#stream-processing-workspaces) supported regions. |
| `serviceEndpointId` | `string \| null` | No | For AZURE EVENTHUB, this is the [namespace endpoint ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/eventhub/namespaces/get). For AWS CONFLUENT cluster, this is the [VPC Endpoint service name](https://docs.confluent.io/cloud/current/networking/private-links/aws-privatelink.html). |
| `state` | `string \| null` | No | State the connection is in. |
| `vendor` | `string \| null` | No | Vendor that manages the cloud service. The list of supported vendor values is: - AWS -- `MSK` for AWS MSK Kafka clusters -- `CONFLUENT` for Confluent Kafka clusters on AWS -- `KINESIS` for AWS Kinesis Data Streams -- `S3` for AWS S3 -- `LAMBDA` for AWS Lambda - Azure -- `EVENTHUB` for Azure EventHub. -- `CONFLUENT` for Confluent Kafka clusters on Azure -- `AZURE_BLOB_STORAGE` for Azure Blob Storage - GCP -- `CONFLUENT` for Confluent Kafka clusters on GCP -- `PUBSUB` for Google Cloud Pub/Sub **NO |

## X509Authentication

### createDatabaseUserCert

`x509Authentication.createDatabaseUserCert`

Create One X.509 Certificate for One Database User: generates one X.509 certificate for the specified MongoDB user

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.mongodbatlas.api.x509Authentication.createDatabaseUserCert({ groupId: '5f43e7f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718', username: 'app-user' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `groupId` | `string` | Yes | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. |
| `username` | `string` | Yes | Human-readable label that represents the MongoDB database user account for whom to create a certificate. |
| `monthsUntilExpiration` | `number` | No | Number of months that the certificate remains valid until it expires. |



**Output:** `string`
